Endpoint.description:
An address you can talk to: an OpenAPI Path Item or an AsyncAPI Channel.

Unifying the two gives one navigation model, one grouping function and one anchor scheme across a docs site that has both a REST and a WebSocket API.

parameters.description: Shared by every operation here: OAS path-level params, AsyncAPI channel params.

protocols.description: ["https"] for REST, ["wss"] for a WebSocket channel. From the resolved servers.

servers.description: Ids into `ApiIR.servers`. Empty means every server.

view.description:
Which view this content is. The adapter has already applied `projectForView` to the inline structure of `node`, but it cannot reach through a `$ref` — a registry entry is shared by every view, and rewriting it would mean three copies of every type. So the view travels with the content, and renderers pass it on:

    toTree(variant.node, ir, { view: variant.view })

Without this a `$ref`-valued request body shows its readOnly fields.

MessageOperation.description:
An AsyncAPI 3.x operation, or one half of a 2.x publish/subscribe pair.

Keeping operations distinct from channels is what makes 3.x `reply` representable; folding messages into the channel would lose it.

address.description: Where the reply arrives, when it differs from the operation's own channel.
